You also have insights from past train runs, inlined at the start of the task message, and
a wiki at /work/corpus, read-only, that holds the runs they came from. They are not the
answer to this task. The task message lists the past runs most similar to this task.

The wiki has three layers.
- /work/corpus/raw/step-NNNN/ is one past run as it happened.
    metadata.md        its task and outcome
    solver.full.jsonl  one JSON line per turn, numbered from 0
- /work/corpus/compilation/step-NNNN.md is a model's account of that run. The model saw
  only whether the run succeeded or failed. For a failed run it had to guess which turn
  caused the failure, and that guess is often wrong.
- The insights in the task message were drawn from the compilations. One from a failed run
  inherits that guess.
Only the raw turns are certain. Each layer has an _index.md.

Go down when an insight tells you what to do but not exactly how, when it came from a
failed run, or when two insights disagree. Look for the one fact that settles it, such as
{fact_example}, in the run. If the same observation comes back twice in a row, read only
the turns where a past run passed that point. Find runs through an insight's source run,
the lower layers' indexes, or a search by {keyword_hint}. Use the `bash` tool freely:
  grep -rl "{keyword_example}" /work/corpus/compilation /work/corpus/raw | head -n 20
  for s in 0002 0017; do cat /work/corpus/compilation/step-$s.md; done
  /work/tools/actions step-0017      # every turn's action, one line each
  /work/tools/turn step-0017 7 9     # turns 7 to 9 in full: reasoning, action, observation

Memory rules
- Never replay a past run. It started from a different state than this task, even when
  its task reads the same, and steps that worked there fail here.
- Take from a run only a fact you can check against this task, such as {fact_example}.
  Name what differs before you use it.
- From a failed run, take only the action to avoid, never the plan.
